criterion.statement: Averaged over related source/target pairs and seeds, warm-start transfer must reduce target MSE by at least 10% relative to an equal-budget fresh model with the same architecture seed. Unrelated pairs are a negative control and are reported separately.

fairness_controls.budget_note: Target-task epochs are matched; source pretraining compute is reported separately and is not disguised as target budget.

hypothesis: Warm-start transfer helps on related rule pairs and does not show the same advantage on unrelated pairs.
limitations: Relatedness is defined by the synthetic rule family, not by a domain-independent metric.
MSE on a low-dimensional synthetic task is not evidence of human-like structure reuse.
The unrelated-prior control shares the same feature surface, so it isolates rule mismatch rather than input-distribution shift.
research_question: Does prior experience reduce target-task learning cost when the source and target share structure, after matching architecture, seed, data and target epochs?
title: Fair transfer diagnostics across rule pairs
